summary:
Echoes of Exploration is an interactive educational website developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: “Abandoned but Not Forgotten.” It brings the stories and lasting legacies of space exploration hardware to life through an interactive 3D Solar System, mission pages, immersive storytelling, mystery quizzes, and a Discovery Journal.

The project explores three missions: Apollo 11, whose lunar hardware remains at Tranquility Base; NASA’s Spirit rover, which became stranded on Mars after years of scientific exploration; and Voyager 1, which provides a contrast as a spacecraft still travelling through interstellar space. By combining scientific information with interactive experiences, the website encourages visitors to explore what missions leave behind, discover their scientific contributions, and understand that the legacy of exploration continues long after major mission milestones.

This project is important because space exploration is not only about reaching new destinations—it is also about remembering the machines, discoveries, and human achievements that made those journeys possible.
details:
Echoes of Exploration is an interactive educational website created for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten.” It helps visitors discover the stories, scientific contributions, and lasting legacies of space exploration missions through an engaging digital experience.

What does the project do and how does it work?

The website features an interactive 3D Solar System where visitors can explore mission destinations and discover three different mission stories:

Apollo 11: Explore the historic lunar landing and the hardware left behind at Tranquility Base.
Spirit Rover: Discover the journey of NASA's Mars rover, its scientific discoveries, and how it eventually became stranded on Mars.
Voyager 1: Learn about the spacecraft's journey beyond the planets and its continuing mission in interstellar space, offering a contrast to abandoned or stranded hardware.

Each mission has dedicated information and storytelling experiences. Visitors can also test their knowledge through mystery quizzes featuring questions, explanations, and NASA source links. Correct answers earn points, while completing mission mysteries unlocks badges. A Discovery Journal allows visitors to track their progress, with saved progress retained using browser local storage.

Benefits and intended impact

The project makes space exploration history more accessible, interactive, and enjoyable. Instead of presenting information as ordinary articles, it encourages visitors to actively explore, investigate clues, answer questions, and learn through discovery.

Its intended impact is to increase curiosity about planetary exploration, improve awareness of the scientific value of past missions, and help people appreciate the lasting legacy of spacecraft and exploration hardware across the Solar System.

Technologies and tools used

The project was developed as a web application using:

React — building the interactive user interface.
Vite — development environment and build tooling.
JavaScript — application logic and interactions.
Three.js — 3D graphics and Solar System visualization.
React Three Fiber — integrating Three.js with React.
Drei — useful 3D components and helpers.
HTML and CSS — website structure, styling, and responsive layouts.
Browser Local Storage — saving quiz scores and Discovery Journal progress.

What makes the project creative?

Echoes of Exploration combines space science, interactive 3D exploration, storytelling, and gamified learning in one experience. Its three missions represent different kinds of space exploration legacy: hardware left on the Moon, a rover stranded on Mars, and a spacecraft still travelling through interstellar space. This contrast helps visitors understand that not every mission's ending is the same.

Factors considered during development

We considered scientific accuracy, educational value, ease of navigation, accessibility, visual clarity, responsive design, and reliable NASA references. We also aimed to make the experience engaging without sacrificing the accuracy of the historical and scientific information.

Ultimately, Echoes of Exploration reminds us that even when a mission ends or a spacecraft travels beyond our reach, its discoveries and contributions remain part of humanity's story.
